newsitem.title: UK: UK's LASMO sees meeting '97 production goal.
newsitem.headline: UK's LASMO sees meeting '97 production goal.

text.p: Oil and gas company LASMO Plc said on Wednesday it expected to reach its stated production target in 1997 of about 200,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, an increase of some 12 percent over this year's expected level.

"This level of production is forecast to be maintained for the next five years from the planned development of existing fields and discoveries under appraisal, principally in Algeria and the UK," the company said in a statement.
During this period, LASMO's capital expenditure on developments was expected to average about 200 million stg per year, the company added.
The group said the developments were in line with its objective of raising shareholder value and growing a business which maintained profitability at low prices.
Joe Darby, chief executive, made the comments in a statement which said discovery costs for the last three years, including 1996, averaged at one stg per barrel.
He concluded that the group had 14 field discoveries under or awaiting development and the group was in a strong position to add value for shareholders into the next century.
